method: Re-attributed the base trace pkj3o (nightTR-6861894f3c-8579e2c221) with a corrected rule (agent2/night/scratch/A042/att.mjs): A2Trace logs bytes [IP-4, IP+6) and IP is the after-fetch IP, so for dwell deaths (DI = anchor+1) the fatal instruction is [DI-1, IP) and its newest foreign writer is the killer. Then tested the lattice-consistency question directly: B-only variants that put captured zombies on their own anchor lattice while B's main path stays rev0 (phoenix_init: dead mov dx,[4A17h] -> lea dx,[bp+0FFBh]; and dx,0 / or dx,0FFBh -> and dx,00FFh / or dh,0Fh, same 11 bytes and instruction count; main path BP=0 gives FAR_SEG 0FFBh; zombie_entry mov bp low byte K gives FAR_SEG 0FFBh+K). Builder agent2/night/scratch/A042/mk.sh; analysis helpers zk.mjs, zp.mjs, att.mjs.

candidates.label: z62 (captured zombies on lattice 62h, 10h above A/B)
candidates.change: B only: zombie_entry mov bp,3400h -> 3401h and mov bp,2000h -> 2001h (AX unchanged because mov al,0A2h follows); phoenix_init mov dx,[4A17h] -> lea dx,[bp+0FFBh], and dx,0 -> and dx,00FFh, or dx,0FFBh -> or dh,0Fh. Zombies run with FAR_SEG 0FFCh (CS word FC 0F); A and B main path unchanged.
candidates.groupNotes: cand 0.5743 vs base 0.6456, W/L 12/31; 2025 -0.0513 [-0.094,-0.009]; strong -0.2675 [-0.451,-0.084] 0/7; threat -0.0288; multi +0.025. Trace xsvgz: captured zombies killed at their anchor by B's bytes 27 (base 1); A+B deaths 166 (base 161). Rejected.

candidates.change: B only: zombie_entry mov bp,3400h -> 33FFh and mov bp,2000h -> 1FFFh (same AX except band 0, which starts 100h lower); same phoenix_init encoding as z62. Zombies run with FAR_SEG 0FFAh (CS word FA 0F).

candidates.label: z00 (control, not screened)
candidates.change: Same encoding with K=0 (mov bp,2000h/3400h kept): behaviour identical to rev0 on all paths. Built only to document that the encoding is neutral (byte diff vs rev0 B: 11 bytes in phoenix_init only).

threatFindings.threat: Captured-zombie trails kill A/B anchors or workers in rev0 (zombies on the partners' 52h lattice)
threatFindings.evidence: Corrected attribution of base trace pkj3o (168 battles, 161 deaths): A/B killed by bytes of our captured zombies 0 in steady state and 1 at startup (s2025-1 w12 r52: captured zom20b trail A4 E8 FB 0F over B's phoenix_init code, the B059 case). The other 'zombie' A/B kills are wild zombies (zom20c/zom20d fixed writes on B's startup code, 3) or a zom20b captured by an opponent's MOVSW phoenix (Baltika9 cohort, trail A5 F2 05 10). Internal kills overall: A <- B 2 (rebuild-window crossfire), zombie <- A 1, zombie <- B 1.
threatFindings.impact: Nothing to fix on this axis in rev0; at most about 1 death per 160 battles.

threatFindings.threat: Earlier counts of zombie/partner kills (A035 ana.mjs: B <- zombie 6, captured zombies <- A/B 13) and the B051 trace note
threatFindings.evidence: agent2/tools/java/A2Trace.java writes bytes for k = -4..5 around CS:IP, and IP is the after-fetch IP (dwell deaths have DI = anchor+1 with IP = anchor+4 for FF A5 xx xx, or anchor+2 for 2-byte faults). ana.mjs takes bytes[0] (IP-4) as the fatal byte, which is correct only for 4-byte fatal instructions. Re-attribution with att.mjs on pkj3o: B <- our zombies 1 (not 6), captured zombies <- A/B 2 (not 13; e.g. MOV_AX_WIN2's FF FF at anchor+1 had been credited to B's old trail bytes at anchor-2). The B051 note 'bytes[] starts at the faulting instruction, not IP-4' is reversed.
threatFindings.impact: Tool caveat for trace-based attributions of 1-3 byte fatal instructions; use agent2/night/scratch/A042/att.mjs.

threatFindings.threat: Captured zombies on a lattice 10h BELOW the partners kill A/B
threatFindings.evidence: z42 trace cwax5: A <- zombie 31 (30 in rebuild), B <- zombie 20 (17 in rebuild); typical fatal bytes 4F FF 1F CC 00 00 00 = the tail of the zombie's own rebuild. The rebuild writes 21 bytes (movsb + movsw + 9 words) from anchor+1 to anchor+21, the last 3 being private-memory zeros, so a zombie anchored 10h below overwrites A/B's anchor+2..+5 while A/B is rebuilding. Screen 6450b ALL -0.170, 2/46.
threatFindings.impact: Explains the 10h-undercut mechanism (the lower rebuild overwrites the upper's starting rebuild). Zombies must never sit below the partner lattice.

threatFindings.threat: Captured zombies on a lattice 10h ABOVE the partners are killed by B
threatFindings.evidence: z62 trace xsvgz: captured zombies killed at their anchor by B-written bytes 27 (base 1), with fatal words like B4 44 FB 0F (B's first push of a generation: return IP = worker call + 2, low byte B4) landing on the zombie anchor; A/B deaths unchanged (166 vs 161). Screen a2r69 ALL -0.071, strong -0.267 (0/7).
threatFindings.impact: Zombie value (about 0.07 points per battle here) is lost when B undercuts its own zombies.

threatFindings.threat: Family/lattice consistency between captured zombies and partners
threatFindings.evidence: rev0 (zombies on 52h, same family) has about 0 internal zombie/partner kills; plus or minus 10h costs -0.071 and -0.170 on the screen (a2r69, 6450b), with mechanisms confirmed in traces xsvgz and cwax5.
threatFindings.impact: The base is already at the consistent point. Any future zombie edit must keep FAR_SEG 0FFBh and the MOVSB residue.

recommendation: Do not promote z62 or z42 (both clearly negative). No fix is needed for captured-zombie vs partner kills in rev0: with corrected attribution they are about 1 per 160 battles. Keep captured zombies on the partners' lattice (FAR_SEG 0FFBh); this also answers A012's card (an offset lattice for zombies costs -0.07 to -0.17). Re-check earlier trace-based claims that used ana.mjs or bytes[0] for 1-3 byte fatal instructions (A035, B059 helpers) with agent2/night/scratch/A042/att.mjs.
notes: The z42/z62 encoding (lea dx,[bp+0FFBh]; and dx,00FFh; or dh,0Fh) gives captured zombies a different FAR_SEG at no size or turn cost, should a zombie-only far segment be needed later.
